subsystems.name: Ribbon
subsystems.role: the load-bearing element: a flat, paper-thin ribbon rather than a round cable, tapered so it is widest near geostationary altitude where tension peaks.
parts: interwoven cross-strands to stop crack spread
coating against atomic oxygen and ultraviolet light

subsystems.name: Anchor and base station
subsystems.role: holds the bottom end at the equator, where the cable hangs vertically.

subsystems.name: Counterweight
subsystems.role: tensioned mass beyond geostationary orbit that keeps the ribbon taut; often conceived as surplus cable or a captured asteroid.

subsystems.name: Climbers
subsystems.role: crawler vehicles that grip the ribbon and carry payload from the surface outward.

subsystems.name: Power delivery
subsystems.role: energises climbers without heavy onboard fuel — usually a ground laser aimed at their solar panels.

subsystems.name: Tracking and avoidance
subsystems.role: keeps the ribbon from being cut.
parts: small thrusters to nudge the ribbon aside

buildSteps.title: Make the fibre
buildSteps.detail: Grow carbon nanotubes or boron nitride nanotubes with very few defects and near-perfect alignment — the step nobody can yet do at length.

buildSteps.title: Spin the ribbon
buildSteps.detail: Tens of millions of parallel strands would be drawn and bonded into a continuous, paper-thin ribbon using a method closer to composite pultrusion than textile weaving.

buildSteps.title: Launch a seed ribbon
buildSteps.detail: Because a full ribbon cannot be lifted, a very thin, light version would be carried to geostationary orbit and spooled out.

buildSteps.title: Deploy both directions
buildSteps.detail: The ribbon is paid out downward toward the equator and outward to the counterweight, while the whole assembly is spun up to orbital rate.

buildSteps.title: Thicken the ribbon
buildSteps.detail: Climbers travelling up and down add further strands, layer by layer, until the ribbon reaches its design cross-section.

buildSteps.title: Attach the anchor
buildSteps.detail: The lower end is captured at an equatorial base and mechanically tied to the ground or a sea platform.

buildSteps.title: Fit the counterweight
buildSteps.detail: Mass is added beyond geostationary orbit to bring the ribbon to its working tension.

buildSteps.title: Begin climbing
buildSteps.detail: Climbers carry payloads outward, releasing them at the altitude whose orbital velocity matches the destination.

buildSteps.title: Operate and defend
buildSteps.detail: A permanent tracking service watches for debris and micrometeoroids, and the ribbon is periodically repaired or replaced strand by strand.

prerequisites.why: the ribbon needs a specific strength of roughly 30–50 GPa·cm³/g; individual nanotubes can in theory approach it, but fibres made from them reach only a few GPa·cm³/g.
strength collapses at the first flaw, and a working ribbon may be 100,000 km long in one continuous piece.
climbers cannot carry enough chemical fuel; ground-based lasers or microwaves must drive them.
any object crossing the ribbon at orbital speed can sever it.

prerequisites.tech: Large-scale in-orbit assembly and launch capacity
prerequisites.why: the seed ribbon, counterweight and climbers all have to be placed in orbit.

prerequisites.tech: Materials durability in the upper atmosphere and vacuum
prerequisites.why: atomic oxygen, ultraviolet light and thermal cycling degrade thin structures.

pathway.milestone: laboratory fibres of carbon nanotubes with strengths of a few GPa over centimetre lengths
pathway.unlocks: a baseline to scale up, but still two orders of magnitude short.

pathway.milestone: metre-to-kilometre continuous nanotube ribbon with high retained strength
pathway.unlocks: credible engineering studies and small-scale tether experiments in orbit.

pathway.milestone: a deployed subscale tether in low Earth orbit, used to lift small payloads part of the way
pathway.unlocks: real data on debris, wear and climber traction.

pathway.milestone: a full geostationary-anchored ribbon with counterweight and laser-powered climbers
pathway.unlocks: payload delivery to orbit without rockets, at a fraction of the energy cost — if the material problem is ever solved.
